newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to stop making minicars--paper.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to stop making minicars--paper.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp will stop producing minicars, cars with engines of 660cc or smaller, in the autumn of next year, Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday.
Mazda spokesmen were not immdiately available for comment on the report.

The paper said the decision was made in view of the Transport Ministry's revision in standards for minicars, taking effect in October 1998, under which it would allow carmakers to produce longer and wider minicars than existing models.
Mazda thinks developing models to meet the new standards would be too costly and it has decided to stop production of minicars, the paper said.

Instead, Mazda will procure minicars from Suzuki Motor Corp and sell them under its own brand name, the paper said. Mazda already has such a sales arrangement with Suzuki regarding recreational and commercial vehicles, it said.
Suffering from an operating loss, Mazda, which is 33.3 percent owned by Ford Motor Co of the United States, is now restructuring. Mazda has made minicars since 1960.
